key_insight: FREDI combines fair wireless resource allocation with dual-threshold early-exit inference so edge devices can quickly handle easy cases and securely escalate critical events for deeper analysis. The result is a cooperative UE–edge–cloud system that improves efficiency without sacrificing security or fairness.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of running real-time AI inference on resource-constrained edge devices while balancing latency, communication cost, security, and fairness across users and network resources.
method: Each UE runs an early-exit CNN with two confidence thresholds to decide whether to accept a prediction locally or flag a case as critical.
Critical events are securely offloaded to an edge server for more detailed classification, reducing unnecessary cloud communication.
A proportional-fair optimization framework allocates wireless and compute resources across the UE–edge–cloud system to balance performance among users.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it offers a practical blueprint for deploying inference at the edge with lower latency and better resource use. It is especially useful for safety- or security-sensitive applications where uncertain predictions should be escalated reliably.

paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
paper_authors: Thai T. Vu, John Le, Tu N. Nguyen, Jun Shen, Quang Vinh Duong
